name: Chip formation
kb: The chip, built-up edge, and shear plane
note: The invention is understanding that metal removal is a shear process at the tool face, not a crushing. Built-up edge is a protective phenomenon, not a defect. Chip curl and control is geometry, not magic.

name: Rake and clearance angles
kb: Single-point tool geometry for turning
note: Rake reduces cutting force and heat; clearance allows the tool to enter without rubbing. The tradeoff is tool strength. Geometry alone saves 30 percent power and doubles tool life.

name: Carbon steel cutting tools
kb: Annealed and hardened carbon steel tooling
note: Carbon steel, hardened and tempered blue, works to about 500 C tool face before softening catastrophically. Mushet steel adds tungsten and vanadium to push this to 600 C, but is expensive and brittle.

name: Mushet steel tooling
kb: Self-hardening tungsten-vanadium tool steel
note: Air-hardens without quenching. Holds hardness to 600 C, double the speed of carbon steel. The speed gain does not come free: breakage is higher and geometry must be precise.

name: High speed steel research
kb: Taylor-White heat treatment for tungsten-cobalt-vanadium alloys
note: The invention is empirical: tool steel with tungsten, molybdenum, vanadium and cobalt, heated red-hot then air-cooled in a specific way. Cuts three times faster than Mushet, holds hardness to 1000 C. Taylor and White took years of trial and measurement to find the window.

name: High speed steel tools
kb: HSS in production use for turning and milling
note: At HSS speed, traditional cast-iron machines shake and tool holders break. A whole infrastructure must rebuild: more rigid machines, more balanced spindles, better bearings. The bottleneck is not the tool, it is the platform.

name: Stellite tools
kb: Cobalt-chromium-tungsten cast alloy
note: Cast at high temperature as a powder-sintered alloy. Harder than HSS but more brittle. Holds hardness to 1200 C. Used for roughing where speed matters more than tool life.

name: Brazed tool tip
kb: Carbide or stellite brazed to a steel shank
note: Brazing carbide tips directly to steel has a thermal expansion mismatch that causes failure. The invention is using a brass layer that stretches to absorb the difference without cracking.

name: Cemented carbide
kb: Tungsten carbide in cobalt binder, powder sintered
note: Tungsten carbide is hard at 1500 C. Cobalt binder keeps it from shattering. The tooling is not steel: it is ceramic sintering, which demands vacuum furnace or inert atmosphere. Cost is ten times HSS, but speed gain is five times and tool life is infinite until breakage.

name: Indexable insert
kb: Throw-away carbide inserts in a precision holder
note: The breakthrough is geometric: chipbreaker geometry cast into the carbide die itself. When one edge dulls, rotate the insert. No resharpening. Tool room cost drops to nearly zero.

name: Cutting speed and feed
kb: Optimising surface speed and feed rate
note: Speed is not instinctive: go too fast and the tool melts, too slow and it wears by diffusion. The rule is empirical and depends on tool material, workpiece material, and coolant. Taylor measured hundreds of cuts to find the relationship.

name: Cutting fluid
kb: Oil, water, or emulsion coolant
note: Oil cools and lubricates the chip and tool. Tallow smokes less but is slower. Water-based emulsion is dangerous because it causes sudden tool failure, but is cheaper. The right choice depends on the material and speed.

name: Engine lathe
kb: Spindle, carriage, compound slide rest, chucks
note: An engine lathe NEEDS cap_tol_10um to build itself (lead screw, spindle bearings). Once built, it MAKES cap_tol_100um easily and cap_tol_10um with care. The spindle is the constraint: runout comes from bearing play and spindle sag.

name: Turret lathe
kb: Turret head with multiple tools, powered indexing
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um and cap_tol_100um. MAKES cap_tol_100um reliably. The turret lets one worker load stock and walk away for a complex sequence: bore, face, part off, repeat. Each job needs a new setup, which takes hours.

name: Automatic screw machine
kb: Cam-driven automatic with cam lobe sequencing
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um to cut the control cams accurately. MAKES cap_tol_100um and sometimes cap_tol_10um. Once programmed by the cam, runs untended. Setup time is days. Scrap rate from cam error is the problem.

name: Multi-spindle automatic
kb: Six or eight independent spindles, one cam
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um for spindle indexing and cam cutting. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Six pieces in work at once means sixfold throughput. The spindles must run in exact synchrony or they jam and break.

name: Vertical jig borer
kb: Vertical spindle, XY table, precision boring for jigs and fixtures
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle runout, XY precision). MAKES cap_tol_10um. Used to bore holes in jigs and tooling to high precision. The table must move in a straight line within 0.01 mm over a metre.

name: Horizontal jig borer
kb: Horizontal spindle for deep boring, better for chip clearance
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_10um. Better for deep holes because the spindle sits level and chips fall freely. Symmetry is harder to hold because the bar cantilevered is longer.

name: Radial drill
kb: Drilling head on a radial arm, table fixed
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (spindle runout). MAKES cap_tol_100um. One operator can drill dozens of holes in a large casting without moving the casting. The radial arm means the spindle can reach anywhere.

name: Shaper
kb: Reciprocating cutting, flat or shaped surfaces
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (table flatness, side clearance). MAKES cap_tol_100um. Uses a single-point tool in a long stroke, slower than milling but simple. The table must move in a dead-flat plane or surfaces will be concave.

name: Planer
kb: Open-side planer for large flat surfaces
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (bed flatness and alignment). MAKES cap_tol_100um easily. The workpiece is fixed and the tool head moves over it. For surfaces larger than a shaper can reach.

name: Slotter
kb: Vertical reciprocating tool for slots and keyways
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Vertical stroke cuts keyways, T-slots, and internal keyways that a shaper cannot reach. The stroke must be perfectly vertical.

name: Universal milling machine
kb: XY table, vertical or horizontal spindle, indexing head
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle, table travel). MAKES cap_tol_100um and cap_tol_10um with care. The table can be tilted, the spindle can be vertical or horizontal, the arbor can be extended. Dozen operations without setup.

name: Horizontal milling machine
kb: Spindle axis horizontal, XY and Z table feeds
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_100um easily. The horizontal spindle reaches into deep pockets. Face milling and end milling on the same machine. Simpler than universal mill, less flexible.

name: Vertical milling machine
kb: Spindle axis vertical, XY table, Z depth
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um. MAKES cap_tol_100um. Better sightlines than horizontal. Pockets and cavities are simpler because the tool is directly above. Less powerful than horizontal for heavy cuts.

name: Profile milling machine
kb: Pantograph or CNC follower for complex profiles
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (follower accuracy). MAKES cap_tol_100um. A tracer head follows a template or master while the cutter follows. Cam lobes, turbine blades, gear teeth. Setup is slow, production is fast.

name: Gear hobbing machine
kb: Hob cutter indexing with gear blank for continuous cutting
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle sync, index precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gears. The hob is a worm gear; as it turns, the workpiece indexes automatically. Tooth form is a spiral, not a straight line.

name: Gear shaper
kb: Reciprocating gear-shaped cutter and workpiece indexing
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (runout, index precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gears. The cutter is shaped like a gear; it reciprocates in mesh with the workpiece. Slower than hobbing but simpler, better for internal gears.

name: Gear grinding machine
kb: Grinding wheel index-synchronized with gear blank
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (spindle, index). MAKES cap_tol_1um on tooth flanks. Used to grind gears after hardening. Heat-treat distortion is corrected. Tooth surface is smooth, low noise.

name: Broaching machine
kb: Long tool with multiple teeth, linear pull through workpiece
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (tool precision). MAKES cap_tol_100um on internal shapes. Keyways, splines, and complex internal profiles in one stroke. The broach pulls through the hole; each tooth cuts 0.1 mm. High force, one pass only.

name: Surface grinder
kb: Rotating wheel, flat magnetic or vacuum chuck
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle runout, bed flatness). MAKES cap_tol_10um easily and cap_tol_1um with care. The workpiece rides on a chuck. Wheel dresses itself or is dressed manually. Parallelism is automatic.

name: Cylindrical grinder
kb: Rotating wheel grinding OD of rotating part
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle, workhead and tailstock centers). MAKES cap_tol_10um easily and cap_tol_1um with practice. The workpiece rotates between centers; the wheel traverses along it. Roundness depends on center alignment.

name: Centreless grinder
kb: Grinding wheel and regulating wheel, no centers
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (wheel axes alignment). MAKES cap_tol_10um. The workpiece floats between the wheels, supported only by grinding pressure. No setup needed; feed parts in continuously. Taper control is by tilting the regulating wheel.

name: Internal grinder
kb: Grinding wheel on spindle inside rotating bore
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (spindle, wheel runout). MAKES cap_tol_10um and cap_tol_1um with care. The wheel spins at high speed inside a bore. Clearance is tight. Used for hardened bearing bores and cylinder walls.

name: Tool and cutter grinder
kb: Grinder with work-holding fixtures for tool resharpening
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (fixtures, wheel trueness). MAKES cap_tol_100um on tools. The fixture holds the tool at the correct angle for rake, clearance, flank relief. Critical for tool sharpening because geometry is not forgiving.

name: Honing machine
kb: Abrasive stone, low speed, high pressure, cross-hatch pattern
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (bore precision before honing). MAKES cap_tol_1um. Honing follows grinding to correct distortion and improve finish. The stone conforms to bore geometry; pressure and stone grade control stock removal.

name: Lapping machine
kb: Abrasive paste, soft tool, slow speed, optical feedback
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (initial precision). MAKES cap_tol_100nm on flat surfaces and mirrors. Lapping removes only 0.001 mm per hour. Used for optical flats and gauge blocks. The operator checks progress by interference bands.

name: Superfinishing machine
kb: Honing stone vibrating at high frequency, minimal traverse
note: NEEDS cap_tol_1um (initial bore). MAKES cap_tol_100nm on cylinder walls and bearing journals. The stone vibrates in place while the bore rotates slowly. Surface finish becomes mirror-smooth.

name: Sawing machine
kb: Band or reciprocating frame saw for cutting bar stock
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (blade tension, guide precision). MAKES no precision requirement. The saw must not deflect or wander. A dull blade generates heat and burns the cut.

name: Shearing machine
kb: Guillotine or rotating blades for sheet and strip
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (blade clearance, table flatness). MAKES straight edges. The blade angle prevents shock. Clearance between blades must be exact or the shear is rough.

name: Punch press
kb: Vertical toggle or screw press with punches and dies
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision, table flatness). MAKES holes to die tolerance. Punches must be hardened and precisely ground. Clearance between punch and die is critical for clean holes.

name: Press brake
kb: Hydraulic or mechanical press with bend dies
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die parallelism). MAKES bend angles to die specification. Springback depends on material and thickness. A mechanical stop on the ram controls bend depth.

name: Hydraulic press
kb: Fluid amplifier, accumulator, directional valve
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (seal precision, valve lands). MAKES large force over small displacement. Leakage is the killer; seals must be tight and piston rod concentricity within 0.1 mm.

name: Drop hammer
kb: Gravity drop with guided dies, mechanical ejection
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die alignment, frame rigidity). MAKES die tolerance. No precision mechanism; it is all gravity and inertia. The frame must be massive to avoid vibration.

name: Forging press
kb: Screw or toggle press for controlled forging
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision). MAKES forgings to die shape. Stroke and pressure must be repeatable. The dies heat from forging; life is limited.

name: Upsetter
kb: Automatic heading machine for bolts and fasteners
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (station precision). MAKES headed bolts to tolerance. Wire is fed, cut, and headed in one machine. The header dies close around the wire and the ram rises through them.

name: Roll former
kb: Powered rollers forming angles, channels, tubes
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (roll concentricity). MAKES formed sections to roll profile. Multiple roll stations bend progressively. The feed rate and roll gap control the final shape.

name: Spinning lathe
kb: Lathe with wooden stake for metal spinning
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (spindle runout). MAKES pressed forms, no precision requirement. The workpiece rotates at low speed; the artisan uses a hand tool and stake to flow the metal. Skill and timing are everything.

name: Deep drawing press
kb: Press with blankholder and guided draws
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (punch and die precision, blankholder pressure). MAKES drawn shells. The blankholder prevents wrinkling in the flange. The die and punch must be polished to reduce friction.

name: Wire drawing bench
kb: Powered draw with carbide or steel dies
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die concentricity). MAKES round wire to diameter tolerance. The die must be hard and the wire must be annealed between draws or it breaks. Emeritus is the traditional die material.

name: Extrusion press
kb: High-temperature hydraulic press for aluminum and steel
note: NEEDS cap_tol_100um (die precision, container alignment). MAKES extruded sections. The workpiece is forced through a shaped die. Temperature control is critical; too cold and it breaks, too hot and it flows unpredictably.

name: Collet chuck
kb: Tapered split sleeve for holding round work
note: Collet grip depends on taper angle and pull distance. A 5-degree taper holds round bar within 0.01 mm runout. Spring back in the sleeve means one pull distance only.

name: Three-jaw chuck
kb: Radial scroll jaw chuck with self-centering
note: The scroll is a spiral groove; rotating the key slides all three jaws in or out simultaneously. Concentricity is within 0.1 mm. Jaw inserts are replaceable.

name: Four-jaw chuck
kb: Independent jaw chuck, manually indexed
note: Four independent jaws are turned by hand-tightened keys. Setup is slower but concentricity can be dial-indicated to 0.01 mm. Better for irregular workpieces.

name: Magnetic chuck
kb: Electro or permanent magnet holding
note: For grinding and milling only; the piece must be magnetic steel. Flat magnetic chucks hold to within 0.05 mm runout. Switching on and off takes seconds.

name: Mandrel
kb: Tapered or threaded spindle for holding bores
note: A simple tapered shaft; the workpiece bores are pressed onto it. Runout depends on bore tolerance and taper fit. Expanding mandrels use a tapered sleeve inside the bore.

name: Arbor
kb: Spindle for mounting cutters between centers
note: A shaft held in the spindle, stepped to fit different cutter bores. Runout at the cutter is critical. Often uses a tapered nose for indexable tools.

name: Indexing head
kb: Precise indexed spindle for milling flats and gears
note: A worm and wheel drive indexed by a pin in a circle of holes. Divisions are exact; an 80-tooth wheel and 40-tooth worm gives 160 positions. Universal heads tilt for helical work.

name: Rotary table
kb: Continuous or indexed rotation, larger than indexing head
note: A heavy cast table with T-slot and dial. Worm and wheel indexing or continuous servo drive. Used for large castings and forgings where an indexing head cannot reach.

name: Die set
kb: Punch and die mounted in guide posts
note: Guide posts and bushings keep punch and die aligned. Clearance between punch and die is the specification. Die sets are modular; the press changes only the top and bottom dies.

name: Progressive die
kb: Multiple stations on one press stroke
note: The strip indexes one station per stroke: blank, pierce, draw, trim, form. One operator feeds stock. Setup is expensive but production is fast and scrap is low.

name: Compound die
kb: Pierce and blank in one stroke
note: The blank punch and trim punch are on one ram; the strip is pierced and blanked simultaneously. Pressure must be balanced or the part shifts and the hole is off-center.

name: Casting mould
kb: Sand mould packed around a pattern
note: The mould is made of compacted sand held in a flask. A pattern is pressed into the sand and withdrawn, leaving a cavity. The core sits inside and defines internal holes.

name: Core box
kb: Precision mould for foundry cores
note: Cores are made separately, baked, and dropped into the mould cavity. The core box defines the core shape; precision here determines hole accuracy. Cores are more expensive than sand.

name: Pattern and shrinkage allowance
kb: Wooden or metal pattern sized for shrinkage
note: Iron shrinks about 0.5 percent as it cools. The pattern is made 0.5 percent larger. Brass shrinks 0.3 percent. If the pattern is wrong, every casting from it is wrong.

name: Go/no-go gauge
kb: Simple pass-fail limit gauges
note: Two gauges: one that must fit, one that must not. Simpler than a micrometer, faster on the floor. Accuracy is binary, not analog. Used for inspection at the machine.

name: Plug gauge
kb: Cylindrical or tapered go-no-go gauge for holes
note: Two plugs: one slightly smaller (go), one slightly larger (no-go). The hole must accept the go and reject the no-go. Simple and fast.

name: Ring gauge
kb: Cylindrical go-no-go gauge for shafts
note: Two rings: one slightly larger (go), one slightly smaller (no-go). The shaft must fit the go and be rejected by the no-go. Worn hand tools are checked this way.

name: Snap gauge
kb: Spring-loaded sliding gauge for external dimensions
note: Two adjustable anvils on a spring handle. Fast inspection of diameters, widths, thicknesses. Feel is everything; training is needed for reproducibility.

name: Thread gauge
kb: Pitch and form go-no-go for screws
note: Checks both pitch and form. Go and no-go rings or plugs. Thread gauges are more expensive than plug or ring gauges because the form must be cut exactly.

name: Height gauge
kb: Precision vertical measurement with vernier scale
note: Measures height above a flat surface to 0.1 mm. Used with an angle plate to check dimensions on irregular parts. Needs a flat reference surface.

name: Sine bar
kb: Two cylinders exactly 100 or 200 mm apart, ground parallel
note: Tilting a sine bar sets an angle precisely using shim stack height and trig. Checks angular tolerances. Cylinders must be ground concentric and parallel to 0.01 mm.

name: Dial indicator
kb: Mechanical gauge with 0.01 mm readability
note: Lever and pinion mechanism converts 0.01 mm motion to one full rotation of the dial. Used to check runout, alignment, parallelism. Repeatability is 0.01 mm but linearity is poor past range.

name: Comparator
kb: Lever amplifier for 0.001 mm readability
note: A lever and pivot system magnifies dial motion 10 or 100 fold. Reads 0.001 mm easily. Used for quality inspection and machine calibration. Sensitivity requires a light touch.

name: Air gauge
kb: Pneumatic pressure differential gauge for holes and bores
note: Compressed air flows through a restrictive jet into the bore. Pressure is read on a gauge. Size is inferred from pressure. Fast and non-contact; used for 100 percent inspection. Settable to 0.01 mm.

name: Optical comparator
kb: Projection of magnified profile on ground glass
note: Illuminated workpiece cast onto ground glass at 50x magnification. Check holes, threads, edge radius, form. Accuracy is limited by light diffraction. Used for tool inspection and quality audits.

name: Tolerance and limit system
kb: Defined limit sizes and fits for interchangeable parts
note: Basic, deviation, upper limit, lower limit. Fits are loose, normal, tight. Code them once in a standard book. Every drawing references the book. Variation is managed by tolerance, not by selection.

name: Control chart
kb: X-bar and R chart for process monitoring
note: Plotted means and ranges show when process is drifting. Samples of five parts, measured every hour. Chart is hand-drawn. When average moves outside control limits, stop and adjust. Saves scrap.

name: Sampling inspection
kb: Lot acceptance by sampling rather than 100 percent
note: Specified sample size and acceptance number. If defects exceed limit, reject the lot. Faster than 100 percent inspection. Risk is quantified: alpha and beta errors.

name: Hot riveting
kb: Heated rivet, set by impact
note: Rivet is heated red-hot, inserted into aligned holes, and upset by a hammer or press. Stronger than cold riveting. Skill is needed to heat correctly without burning.

name: Cold riveting
kb: Cold rivet driven by punch and die
note: Cold is weaker than hot but faster. Used for thin sheet and small fasteners. Die must be tight or the rivet head is deformed.

name: Forge welding
kb: Heat to cherry-red and hammer together
note: Borax flux prevents oxidation. Pieces must reach the same temperature or the joint will crack. Skill is high; success rate for large joints is 70 percent.

name: Oxy-acetylene welding
kb: Neutral flame from oxygen and acetylene
note: Melts steel and fills the gap with filler rod. Speed and quality depend on flame control. Overheating causes carbon loss and brittleness. Cooling rate must be slow or cracks form.

name: Arc welding with bare electrode
kb: Bare steel electrode and direct current power supply
note: Arc melts both electrode and base metal. Metal oxides form and contaminate the weld. Bare weld is porous and brittle. Later, coated electrodes cover this defect.

name: Arc welding with coated electrode
kb: Electrode coated with flux to shield the arc
note: Flux shields the arc and produces a slag that protects the molten metal. The slag is chipped off after cooling. Weld is stronger and less porous than bare electrode.

name: Submerged arc welding
kb: Wire and flux submerged under granular flux, automatic
note: Wire feed is automatic; flux is poured on. Arc is invisible beneath the flux. Very clean; minimal spatter. Used for large structural welds. Quality is high but equipment is complex.

name: Resistance spot welding
kb: Pressure and current pulse at copper electrodes
note: Two copper electrodes clamp the sheet. High current for 0.1 seconds melts a nugget. Electrodes must be cooled between welds. Timing and pressure are critical. Used for mass-produced sheet parts.

name: Resistance seam welding
kb: Rotating roller electrodes for continuous seam
note: Rollers rotate and advance at synchronised speed, pulsing current. Creates a sealed seam. Used for tanks and pipes. Overlap of nuggets makes the seam.

name: Flash butt welding
kb: Flashing and upset of rails and rods
note: Two parts are brought together under pressure. Current causes localized melting and expulsion. Parts are then upset together. Used for end-to-end joints in rails and tubes.

name: Brazing
kb: Brass or copper filler, capillary flow into joint
note: Filler melts at 900-1000 C but does not melt the base metal. Strong joint by wetting and capillary action. Flux is essential to remove oxides.

name: Silver soldering
kb: Silver-copper alloy filler for high-strength joints
note: Joint is stronger than soft solder and more ductile than braze. Used for jewelry, instruments, and small precision parts. Gap must be 0.1 mm.

name: Soft soldering
kb: Lead-tin solder at 230 C
note: Filler wets and fills the joint. Weak in shear but adequate for plumbing and sheet-metal seams. Flux prevents oxidation. Must be cleaned after soldering or corrosion occurs.

name: Flux
kb: Chemical to dissolve oxides and promote wetting
note: Borax is best for braze and forge. Rosin is used for electronics. Salt is crude but works. Flux residue must be cleaned or it causes corrosion.

name: Adhesive bonding
kb: Resin or bitumen adhesive for assembly
note: Used for wood and leather. Not for metal under load. Gap-filling is possible but joint is only as strong as the adhesive.

name: Pickling
kb: Acid bath to dissolve oxides
note: Iron parts are soaked in acid after heat-treat or forge. Scale dissolves. Temperature and time control removal rate. Parts must be rinsed immediately or they rust.

name: Shot blasting
kb: Steel shot impacted under force to clean surface
note: Shot is recirculated. Removes scale and rust. Creates compressive stress in the surface, improving fatigue life. Expensive equipment but fast cleaning.

name: Sand blasting
kb: Sand or abrasive under air pressure
note: Cheaper than shot. Faster removal of rust and scale. Health hazard from silica dust. Nozzle wears quickly. Surface finish is rougher.

name: Tumbling
kb: Parts rolling in drums with abrasive media
note: Media is ceramic or steel balls. Slow but gentle. Burrs and sharp edges are removed. Edge radius increases by 0.2 mm. Batch size must be large for economy.

name: Buffing and polishing
kb: Cloth wheel with rouge or paste compound
note: Final finish for inspection or appearance. Removes fine scratches. Does not correct form errors. Labor-intensive; operator skill affects consistency.

name: Electroplating
kb: Electrodeposited coating of copper, nickel, chromium
note: Cathode is the part; anode is the coating metal. Current and duration control thickness. Nickel is 0.02 mm, chromium is 0.01 mm. Pre-cleaning is critical.

name: Anodising
kb: Electrolytic oxidation of aluminum surface
note: Aluminum is the anode; oxide layer grows into the metal. Thickness is 0.01 to 0.1 mm. Can be dyed. Hardness is high; wear resistance is good.

name: Galvanising
kb: Hot-dip or electroplated zinc coating
note: Hot-dip is cheap but uneven. Thickness is 0.05 to 0.1 mm. Flux must be used to prevent oxidation in the bath. Parts are shaken to remove excess.

name: Painting
kb: Brush, spray, or dip application of paint
note: Surface preparation is 80 percent of quality. Dust must be removed. Paint thickness should be even. Multiple coats improve coverage and durability.

name: Enamelling
kb: Fused glass coat on metal by heating
note: Enamel powder is dusted or sprayed onto the part, then heated to 700-900 C. Shrinkage mismatch causes cracking if not managed. Appearance is high gloss.

name: Phosphating
kb: Zinc or iron phosphate coating for paint adhesion
note: Chemical conversion coating, 0.001 to 0.01 mm. Improves paint adhesion and rust resistance. Produces distinctive gray or tan surface. Fast process.

name: Japanning
kb: Glossy black or colored enamel, baked
note: Traditional for machinery. Two or three coats, each baked. Provides protection and appearance. Slower than painting but harder finish.

name: Moving assembly line
kb: Work in progress moves along the line automatically
note: The line speed is set by the slowest station. Balance is critical; idle stations waste capacity. Ford introduced this for automobiles; it requires complete standardisation.

name: Work study
kb: Analysis of methods and motion to eliminate waste
note: Observation identifies unnecessary motion. Methods are redesigned. Work is simplified so skill requirements drop and training is faster. Productivity gains of 20 to 40 percent.

name: Time study
kb: Measurement of cycle time by stopwatch or chronograph
note: Multiple runs, average cycles. Normal pace and foreign elements identified. Accounts for fatigue and personal time. Builds the standard hour.

name: Standard hour
kb: Defined output rate for piece rate or efficiency measurement
note: If standard is 100 pieces per hour and a worker makes 120, efficiency is 120 percent. Used to pay piece rates fairly. Rates must be updated when methods change.

name: Piece rate payment
kb: Payment based on output, not time worked
note: Worker is motivated to speed production. Quality must be monitored separately. Disputes over rate fairness are common. Requires accurate timekeeping and inspection.

name: Production schedule
kb: Planned sequence and quantity of runs
note: Balances demand, inventory, machine loading, and worker availability. Changes mid-month cause chaos. Lead time is built in. Revision cycle is weekly or monthly.

name: Bill of materials
kb: List of all parts and quantities for one finished product
note: Exploded from drawings. Used for procurement and assembly. Must be updated when design changes. One assembly may contain hundreds of parts.

name: Inventory and reorder point
kb: Minimum stock and reorder trigger for materials
note: Reorder point accounts for lead time and usage rate. Too high and money is tied up. Too low and production stops. Manual ledger is slow; calculation is simple arithmetic.

name: Drawing office
kb: Centralized production design and documentation
note: One source of truth. Drawings are issued to shop floor only after approval. Changes are tracked. Library of standard parts. Three draftsmen can support 200 workers.

name: Orthographic projection and drawing conventions
kb: Three views and dimensioning standard for shops
note: Top, front, side views show all dimensions needed. Operator does not interpret; numbers are clear. Standardization means a drawing from one factory is readable anywhere.

name: Dimensioning and tolerancing conventions
kb: Standard notation for limits and tolerances on drawings
note: Defines basic size, deviation, fit type. All operators read from the same playbook. Reduces ambiguity that causes scrap.

name: Blueprint process
kb: Cyanotype contact printing from linen drawing
note: Original is drawn on translucent linen. Contact print on blueprint paper produces white lines on blue. Copies are made at copying house. One master feeds 50 machines.

name: Change order
kb: Formal process to update design mid-production
note: Customer-driven or engineering-discovered. Each change is approved, costed, and scheduled. Affects inventory, work in progress, and tools. Traceability is recorded.

name: Tool room
kb: Centralized facility for tool storage, maintenance and repair
note: Tools are issued by requisition, returned by EOD. Sharpening is scheduled. Inventory is by category. One tool room supports 50 machines.

name: Maintenance department
kb: Preventive and corrective machine maintenance program
note: Scheduled oil changes, bearing checks, belt replacement. Machine breakdowns are catastrophic; prevention is cheaper. Daily rounds by maintenance crew. Spare parts are stockpiled.

name: Quality department
kb: Dedicated inspection and process monitoring team
note: Separate from production to avoid bias. Audits process at machines and in receiving. Finds root causes of defects. Reports to management. Drives continuous improvement.

name: Dividing engine
kb: Worm and wheel precision indexing for gear and screw cutting
note: NEEDS cap_tol_10um (worm pitch, wheel bore). MAKES cap_tol_100um on gear blanks. Accurate gear generation depends on indexing precision. Once calibrated, divisions repeat exactly.

name: Cam lobe profile cutting
kb: Geometric cutting of eccentric profiles for automatic machines
note: Cams control the sequence of operations. Profile error of 0.1 mm causes misfeeds or collisions. Cutting is slow; inspection by optical comparator is essential.

name: Escapement lever mechanism
kb: Ratchet and pawl indexer for cam-driven sequence control
note: Holds position between strokes, advances one station per cycle. Timing must be precise or the next tool collides with work. Spring return must be repeatable.
